name: Display
description: Display-sized heading for marketing hero copy. Larger than the `Title` scale; used sparingly on landing/about/contact heroes where the type itself is the visual.

ariaRequirements: Renders an h1/h2/h3 by default — semantic heading. Override the level via `as` when nesting inside a section that already owns the page h1.
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-05-28 — Bucket-1 beta port: keyboard/ARIA contract reviewed, ForcedColors story added, Storybook axe gate (parameters.a11y.test: error).

as.description: Element to render, defaults to h1

forbiddenUse: Use `Display` for in-page section headings — that is `Title`.
Stack two `Display` headings in the same viewport — the marketing visual collapses.
dense: Hero-scale Satoshi display type: one size above the Title ladder for page heroes and taglines; polymorphic as h1|h2|p|span|div (h1 default) — semantics chosen by placement, scale is fixed

usage.description: Display is the hero-scale text voice — one deliberate step above the Title ladder, for the handful of moments a page leads with type: heroes, campaign taglines, big numbers. The scale is fixed; `as` picks the semantics (`h1` default; use `p`/`span` when the text is decorative rather than the document heading). If you are choosing between sizes, you want Title — Display has exactly one job.

bestPractices.description: Reserve it for one display moment per page — the hero; a page of Displays has no hero.
Match as to the document outline: h1 in the page hero, p or span for decorative taglines near an existing heading.
Constrain the measure (max-width) — display type past ~15 words per line collapses its impact.
Let it wrap naturally; never force line breaks for shape at one viewport.
Do not use Display for section headings — that is the Title ladder (levels decoupled from sizes).
Do not stack Display lines to fake a type ladder; hierarchy below the hero belongs to Title and Text.
